resources.string: Chain
Stack Aether with Psiphon and Tor. More hops means more ways past a filter, and less speed.
Cores
Path: %1$s
Aether
Aether alone. Fastest. Start here and only add hops when this does not get through.
Psiphon
Psiphon alone. Worth trying when it is Cloudflare WARP itself that your network blocks.
Tor
Tor alone. Anonymous, slow, and blocked outright on many networks in Iran.
Psiphon over Aether
Psiphon dials out through Aether. Your operator sees WARP traffic and nothing that looks like Psiphon.
Tor over Aether
Tor reaches the Tor network through Aether. Use this when Tor cannot connect at all, or to hide that you use Tor.
Tor over Psiphon
Tor reaches the Tor network through Psiphon. Use this when Tor is blocked and WARP is blocked too.
Tor over Psiphon over Aether
All three, stacked. The slowest option in the app and the last thing left to try.
Psiphon exit country
e.g. NL
Two-letter country code. Leave empty to let Psiphon pick its fastest server, which is usually the right answer.
Psiphon config (JSON)
{\"PropagationChannelId\": …, \"SponsorId\": …}
Psiphon issues this file; it is not bundled with the app. Leave empty if your build already ships one. See docs/CHAINING.md.
Tor adds three relays: expect much higher latency, and no UDP at all, so video calls and QUIC fall back to TCP or stop working. The first connection can take a few minutes.
Tor exit country
e.g. de
Two-letter country code for the exit relay. Needs the geoip database bundled in the build; leave empty to let Tor choose.
Only that country
Never fall back to another country when the one you chose has no usable exit. That can mean no connection at all.
